title: The Argument Reasoning Comprehension Task: Identification and Reconstruction of Implicit Warrants
authors: Ivan Habernal; Henning Wachsmuth; Iryna Gurevych; Benno Stein
task_description: Choose the correct implicit warrant connecting a reason/premise to a claim from two plausible opposing warrants; the released material also contains authentic arguments, reason spans/gists, and warrant-construction annotations.
inputs: News-comment/debate arguments with topic context, claim, reason, and two candidate warrants
outputs_or_labels: Binary correct-warrant label; warrant versus alternative-warrant pairs; related reason-span/gist annotations and released construction materials
pipeline_gap_filled: implicit-warrant identification and warrant reconstruction with evaluable labels/artifacts
artifact_access_status: Official GitHub repository exposes source code, SemEval data, annotation exports, and documentation
license_status: CC-0 is stated for the alternative-warrant data in the paper/repository; verify file-level licenses before redistribution
evidence_basis: ACL abstract states 1,970 high-quality warrant instances and a two-option warrant-selection task; official repository documents train/dev/test files, labels, and annotation exports.
limitations: Primary task selects between candidate warrants rather than freely generating a single gold premise; known artifact has train/dev/test conventions and possible split/label-order pitfalls.
why_relevant: Strongest established benchmark for implicit warrants: authentic arguments, contrastive distractors, explicit labels, and reproducible files.

title: Implicit Knowledge in Argumentative Texts: An Annotated Corpus
authors: Maria Becker; Michael Staniewski; Vivi Nastase; etc.
benchmark_or_resource_name: Implicit Knowledge in Argumentative Texts / Microtexts extension
task_description: Insert short natural-language information that makes a connection between two argumentative units explicit; annotate the inserted sentence with semantic-clause and ConceptNet knowledge-relation types.
inputs: Pairs of argumentative units from the Microtexts Corpus with existing component/relation annotations
outputs_or_labels: Human-written implicit-knowledge sentences plus semantic clause types and ConceptNet relation labels
pipeline_gap_filled: free-form missing-premise/bridge generation with typed semantic artifacts
artifact_access_status: ACL landing page and paper are accessible; a separate downloadable corpus URL was not verified in retained evidence
license_status: Not stated in retained evidence; do not infer a license from ACL availability
evidence_basis: ACL paper abstract explicitly describes high-quality annotations on Microtexts unit pairs, inserted sentences, clause types, and ConceptNet relations.
limitations: Small and focused corpus; inserted knowledge can be multi-step or relation-like rather than a single Toulmin warrant; artifact URL needs independent confirmation.
why_relevant: Best direct free-generation resource for missing information between explicit argument units, with labels useful for stratified evaluation.

title: Mind the Gap: Automated Corpus Creation for Enthymeme Detection and Reconstruction in Learner Arguments
benchmark_or_resource_name: Learner-argument enthymeme corpus / Mind the Gap
task_description: Detect inadequate implicit argumentative discourse units in learner essays and generate corresponding text that makes the missing premise or conclusion explicit.
inputs: Learner essays from ICLEv3; extracted argumentative discourse units, candidate enthymeme positions, and generated reconstructions
outputs_or_labels: Detected enthymeme positions, premise/claim structure, generated explicit premise or conclusion, and quality-filtering metadata
pipeline_gap_filled: enthymeme detection plus reconstruction in longer authentic argumentative texts
artifact_access_status: ACL paper and PDF accessible; separate corpus/artifact download was not verified in retained evidence
evidence_basis: ACL abstract/search evidence says the work creates a corpus for enthymeme detection and reconstruction, targets learner arguments, and contrasts its setting with the 1,970-instance warrant resource.
limitations: Corpus creation relies on automatic truncation/filtering and generated reconstructions; exact released artifact, split, and human-validation fields require verification before use as a gold benchmark.
why_relevant: Important complementary benchmark to ARCT: longer learner essays, implicit premise/conclusion positions, and reconstruction quality rather than only binary warrant choice.

title: Implicit Premise Generation with Discourse-aware Commonsense Knowledge Models
authors: Tuhin Chakrabarty; Aadit Trivedi; Smaranda Muresan
task_description: Generate the implicit premise of an enthymeme from its stated premise and conclusion, using discourse-aware commonsense modeling; evaluates on ARCT-derived material and two additional datasets.
inputs: Explicit premise and conclusion/enthymeme context from ARCT and related commonsense/abductive datasets
outputs_or_labels: Generated implicit premise; automatic and human evaluation scores across three datasets
pipeline_gap_filled: generation models and evaluation protocols for free-form implicit-premise reconstruction
artifact_access_status: ACL paper and PDF accessible; benchmark artifacts are inherited from component datasets and not all separately verified here
evidence_basis: ACL abstract explicitly defines implicit-premise generation and reports evaluation on three datasets, with discourse-aware commonsense improving automatic and human evaluation.
limitations: This is primarily a modeling/evaluation paper, not a newly released benchmark; inherited datasets differ in task format and should not be merged without provenance-preserving mapping.
why_relevant: Provides practical generation baselines, metrics, and dataset combinations for testing free-form reconstruction after selecting a benchmark resource.

title: A Comparative Study on Collecting High-Quality Implicit Reasonings at a Large-scale
authors: Yunqi Xu; Shanshan Li; Jialong Wu; etc.
task_description: Collect and compare natural-language, user-defined keyword-based, and pre-defined keyword-based warrant annotations for claim-premise pairs, then assess quality with trained experts.
inputs: 600 claim-premise pairs from IBM-Rank-30k across multiple debate topics
outputs_or_labels: Approximately 6,000 warrants; methodology labels; expert-quality judgments and annotation guidelines
pipeline_gap_filled: high-volume warrant collection and quality-control protocol for reconstruction data
artifact_access_status: Paper and preprint are accessible; released data/guidelines link was described but not independently verified in retained evidence
evidence_basis: Abstract states a preliminary dataset of 6,000 warrants over 600 arguments and compares three collection methodologies with expert evaluation.
limitations: Preliminary/ongoing resource; exact final artifact, split, and license need verification; keyword-based warrants may not be directly comparable to natural-language sentence reconstruction.
why_relevant: Useful scale and annotation-method comparator for evaluating whether warrant quality and agreement improve beyond ARCT-style crowdsourcing.

title: A Resource for Enthymeme Detection in Controversial Political Discourse
benchmark_or_resource_name: Enthymeme Detection in Controversial Political Discourse resource
task_description: Detect whether a political-discourse item contains an enthymeme, classify implicit premise versus implicit conclusion versus none, identify argument structure, and reconstruct the missing component under a formal entailment-oriented definition.
inputs: 1,482 annotated political tweets with argument-structure judgments and free-text reconstruction fields
outputs_or_labels: Enthymeme presence/absence; implicit-premise/implicit-conclusion/none labels; argument-slot structure; reconstructed propositional content; annotator disagreement/soft labels
pipeline_gap_filled: formalized enthymeme detection and structurally verifiable reconstruction in political discourse
artifact_access_status: arXiv paper is accessible; dataset artifact/repository was not independently verified in retained evidence
evidence_basis: The arXiv abstract reports 1,482 annotated tweets and explicitly defines reconstruction using implicit components and propositional entailment-oriented structure.
limitations: Published artifact, final version, and license require verification; tweets may have access/deletion constraints; current paper is a preprint and should be version-pinned.
why_relevant: Most direct recent candidate for a benchmark with both detection labels and reconstruction artifacts beyond binary warrant choice; useful for testing premise/conclusion asymmetry and formal validation.

title: Annotating Implicit Reasoning in Arguments with Causal Links
authors: M. Singh; N. Inoue; S. Mim; T. Naitoh; K. Inui
task_description: Annotate causal links that express implicit reasoning between explicit argument components, providing structured supervision for reconstructing argumentative connections.
inputs: Natural-language arguments with explicit argumentative components and latent causal connections
outputs_or_labels: Causal-link spans/relations and associated argument structure annotations
pipeline_gap_filled: structured bridge extraction as an intermediate task between argument mining and free-form warrant generation
artifact_access_status: Preprint is accessible; artifact release/access was not independently verified in retained evidence
evidence_basis: The retained benchmark inventory identifies the paper as an evaluation resource for implicit reasoning with causal-link materials.
limitations: Causal links are not necessarily full natural-language warrants or complete premise reconstructions; exact corpus size, splits, and artifact status require primary-source verification.
why_relevant: Good intermediate benchmark for measuring whether a system recovers an inspectable bridge before attempting unconstrained sentence generation.
